t.7.30.1: When the exceedingly mighty Mahendra had been conquered by the son of Rāvaṇa, the gods then went to Laṅkā, placing Prajāpati at their head.
t.7.30.2: Approaching that Rāvaṇa, who was surrounded by his sons and brothers, Prajāpati, standing in the sky, spoke to him with conciliatory words.
t.7.30.3: Dear child Rāvaṇa, I am pleased with your son in battle. Ah, his valour and nobility! He is your equal, or even greater.
t.7.30.4: Indeed, the entire three worlds have been conquered by you through your own might; the vow you made has borne fruit, and I am truly pleased with your own son.
t.7.30.5: And this exceedingly mighty son of yours, O Rāvaṇa, Rāvaṇi, shall be renowned in the world as Indrajit.
t.7.30.6: This mighty rākṣasa will become a conqueror of enemies; relying on him, O king, you have brought the thirty gods under your control.
t.7.30.7: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, let the great Indra, chastiser of Pāka, be released. And what shall the dwellers of heaven give for his release?
t.7.30.8: Then the mighty and splendid Indrajit, victor in battle, said: "O god, in return for releasing him here, I choose immortality."
t.7.30.9: Then the lotus-born god said to Rāvaṇi: "Complete immortality does not exist for any living beings on earth."
t.7.30.10: Then Indrajit spoke to the Lotus-born one who was present there: "Let it be heard what boon there would be for me in the release of Śatakratu."
t.7.30.11: O god, this is ever my wish: that whenever I, longing to vanquish my enemies, am about to descend into battle, I may first honour the fire with oblations.
t.7.30.12: But if, O god, I should fight in battle while that oblation of muttered prayers to the fire, Vibhāvasu, remains unfinished, then let destruction be my lot.
t.7.30.13: Every man, indeed, chooses immortality through austerity alone; but by me this immortality has been brought about through valour.
t.7.30.14: "So be it," the god Prajāpati said to him in reply. Śakra was released by Indrajit, and the gods went to heaven.
t.7.30.15: Meanwhile, O Rāma, Śakra, dejected, his garments and garlands fallen away, his mind overwhelmed by anxiety, became wholly absorbed in brooding thought.
t.7.30.16: Seeing him in that state, the god Prajāpati said: "O Śatakratu, why do you grieve with longing? Remember your evil deed."
t.7.30.17: O lord of the immortals, O master, long ago I created many beings, all of one colour, of the same speech, and alike in form in every respect.
t.7.30.18: For among them there was no distinction at all, either in appearance or in marks. Then I, with a concentrated mind, reflected upon those creatures.
t.7.30.20: Then I fashioned a woman, Ahalyā, out of the excellences of beauty, and it was I who gave her the name Ahalyā.
t.7.30.19: So I, to make one stand out above them, fashioned a single woman: whatever feature of the creatures was most excellent, each such feature was drawn out and placed in her.
t.7.30.21: But when that woman had been fashioned, O lord of the gods, O bull among the deities, this thought then arose in me: "Whose will she be?"
t.7.30.22: But you, O Śakra, O lord, then regarded that woman in your mind, thinking, 'Because of the superiority of my station, she is my wife,' O Puraṃdara.
t.7.30.23: She was placed by me as a trust with the great-souled Gautama for many years, and she was given back by him.
t.7.30.24: Then, having recognized the steadfastness of that great sage and knowing his perfection in austerity, she was at that time bestowed by me upon him to be his wife.
t.7.30.25: That righteous-souled great sage delighted in her company, but the gods were left without hope once she had been given to Gautama.
t.7.30.26: But you, enraged and driven by lust, went here to the hermitage of that sage, and you then saw that woman, blazing like a tongue of fire.
t.7.30.27: She was violated by you, O Śakra, tormented by desire and inflamed with passion; and you were then seen in the hermitage by that supreme sage.
t.7.30.28: Then you were cursed by that enraged one of supreme splendour, and because of that curse, O lord of the gods, you have suffered a reversal of your condition and fortune.
t.7.30.29: Since my wife was violated by you fearlessly, O Vāsava, therefore, O king, you shall fall into the hands of the enemy in battle.
t.7.30.30: But this condition, O evil-minded one, which you have set in motion here, will without doubt come to exist among all human beings as well.
t.7.30.31: Whatever great and very mighty unrighteousness shall arise there, half of it shall fall on the one who will commit it, and half shall fall upon you.
t.7.30.33: "Whoever becomes the lord of the gods shall not remain secure in that position; this curse has been released by me." Thus did he speak to you at that time.
t.7.30.32: Nor shall your position ever be secure, O Puraṃdara, because of this unrighteous conduct which you have set in motion here.
t.7.30.34: Having severely rebuked that wife of his, the one of very great austerity said: "O ill-behaved woman, be gone, perish far from the vicinity of my hermitage!"
t.7.30.35: Since you, endowed with beauty and youth, have been unsteady, therefore you shall not be the only beautiful woman in the world.
t.7.30.36: And all creatures shall come to share that beauty of yours, so very hard to obtain, since it was on account of it that this delusion arose.
t.7.30.37: From that time onward, creatures have for the most part been endowed with beauty, for all this came about through the curse that sage pronounced.
t.7.30.38: Remember, O mighty-armed one, that evil deed which was done by you, by which, and by nothing else, you fell into the capture of the enemy, O Vāsava.
t.7.30.39: Quickly perform a sacrifice dedicated to Viṣṇu, with your mind well composed; purified by that sacrifice, you will then go to heaven.
t.7.30.40: And your son, O lord of the gods, did not perish in the great battle; he was carried off by Āryaka and kept close at hand in the great ocean.
t.7.30.41: Having heard this, the great Indra performed the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice, then ascended once more to heaven and ruled over the gods.
t.7.30.42: This, O Rāma, is the might of Indrajit which I have recounted: by him the lord of the gods himself was vanquished, so what then of other living beings?
